name: Standard Scramble

waypoints.name: Sol Duc Trailhead (Sol Duc Falls / Sol Duc River Trail, end of Sol Duc Hot Springs Rd)
waypoints.note: Not a direct approach — this is the start of the multi-day Bailey Range Traverse (Sol Duc River Trail -> Heart Lake -> High Divide/Catwalk -> cross-country to Bailey Range), the standard way climbers reach Mount Pulitzer's East Ridge.
waypoints.directions: From Port Angeles, drive about 29 miles west on US 101 and turn left onto Sol Duc Hot Springs Road. Follow it about 14 miles, past the resort, to the trailhead at road's end. A national park entrance pass is required, and an overnight wilderness permit for the traverse.

waypoints.name: Mount Pulitzer summit
waypoints.directions: Follow the Sol Duc River Trail to Heart Lake and the High Divide, then leave maintained trail at the Catwalk below Mount Carrie for the cross-country Bailey Range: sidehill below Carrie and Ruth, drop to Cream Lake and climb into Upper Ferry Basin to camp. From camp, go up to the Ferry-Pulitzer col and scramble the loose Class 3 east ridge to the summit. Plan on two to three days.

descent_text: For an out-and-back side trip from Ferry Basin, reverse the east ridge from the false summit to the Ferry–Pulitzer col and descend to camp. Parties continuing the full Bailey Range Traverse instead push on south off Pulitzer toward Lone Tree Pass and Bear Pass rather than retracing their steps, dropping into Queets Basin en route toward Mount Olympus and the Elwha Snowfinger exit.
